How to edit an AI draft so it sounds like you

An AI draft is a starting point. What makes it yours is the editing, and the edits that matter most are about content, not word choice.

Published 17 November 2026

1. Cut the opening and the closing

Model drafts usually begin by restating the topic and end by summarising what was just said. Delete both and see whether anything is lost. Usually the piece starts better at the second paragraph.

2. Add what only you know

A model writes what is generally true. You know what happened in your lab, your classroom, your business. Put in the actual figure, the name of the place, the thing that went wrong. Specific detail is the clearest difference between generic text and real writing, and it is the part readers remember.

3. Take a position

Drafts tend to balance every point with a counterpoint and conclude that “both have merits”. If you have a view, state it and give your reason. If you do not, say what you would need to know to decide.

4. Break the rhythm

Read the draft aloud. If every sentence is the same length, shorten some and join others. A three-word sentence after a long one is fine. So is a question.

5. Remove stock phrases

“It is important to note that”, “plays a crucial role”, “in today’s fast-paced world”, “a wide range of”: delete them and the sentence nearly always survives. The humanizer on this site does this pass for you and shows each change, which is a quick way to see how many of these a draft contains.

6. Undo the lists of three

Models like triplets: “efficient, scalable and robust”. Keep the one item you can support and drop the other two.

7. Check every fact

Models state wrong things in a confident tone, and invent references. Verify each figure, date, quotation and citation against a source you have opened yourself.

A note on honesty

Editing a draft well does not change where it came from. Many universities, journals and employers now have rules on AI assistance, and most ask you to disclose it. Follow the rule that applies to you. Disclosed, carefully edited AI help is accepted in more and more settings; undisclosed use that breaks a rule is a risk no amount of rewording removes.
